_notes: Configured from the live site (June 2026). BESTCA runs a newer SearchSpring "Snap" storefront theme + CAD pricing, unlike BESTUS. Quirks: category taxonomy is /any-surface-access-doors/... (no /products/ — it 404s); product grid renders into ul.ss__results.ss__results--grid (not ul.productGrid); pagination uses .ss__pagination__* with ?page=2 query param; sort is a custom .ss__dropdown that hash-routes (#/sort:calculated_price:asc); breadcrumbs are plain .breadcrumbs whose links (incl. the Home link) carry a.breadcrumb-label (verified live July 2 2026 — breadcrumbHome filled on plp/pdp selectors; the default .breadcrumb-label >=2 check also applies); sidebar is a single-block .page-sidebar (so the >=2-block sidebar test is skipped via sidebar:null; the category tree is covered by bestSellers #treeView); PDP has no qty stepper buttons; reviews in #yotpo-reviews-main-widget; recently-viewed SearchSpring profile is "similar"; Product JSON-LD is present but priceCurrency is CAD. Qty stepper absence re-verified live July 2 2026 (no button[data-action=inc/dec] in PDP HTML) — qtyIncrement/qtyDecrement stay null. Contact/quote/proClub submitUrlPatterns tightened to named Zoho forms July 2 2026 (BESTCAContactUsNew, BESTCARequestAQuote, BestAccessDoorsProClubCanadaApplication). PRO CLUB (July 14 2026): the live form gained a required country dropdown select[name=Address_Country] (options -Select- / Canada / United States, default -Select-), so hasCountry flipped false->true — the shared persona (country: Canada) now selects Canada and the address validates. The United States option is intentional (routes inattentive US applicants to a post-submit error screen linking to the US Pro Club form), NOT a region-lock deficiency, so no allowedCountries restriction is set. LIGHTHOUSE (calibrated July 2 2026, live scores homepage a11y 70 / plp 78 / pdp 68): Snap theme is structurally below a healthy a11y score, but all clear the fleet-wide accessibility:60 floor (no per-store override).thresholds. July 21 2026: dropped discovery.categories '/exterior-access-doors-and-panels/' — its 3rd product card is a quote-only item (the 24x24 Airtight / Watertight Access Door) with an empty price element, breaking the PLP-grade assertProductCards price check on discovery category pages. Kept the 5 other cats, all verified live with priced first 3 cards. CHECKOUT (onboarded Sept 22 2026): checkout.product is /12-x-12-universal-access-panel/ (SKU BAC-UAP-12-12, product id 3456, $57.99 CAD) — the only slug in pdp.popular that is priced, in stock, purchasable, parcel-sized AND carries zero product-option inputs; verified live to add exactly 1 physical line item. The reliable test is the data-cart-item-add form's inputs, not the rendered page: BESTUS's checkout product looks identical in a browser but carries a required 8-option radio group attribute[6204] (the slam-latch modifier), which is why it adds 2 line items and why the spec compares against a count captured before sign-in rather than a hardcoded 1. Rejected here: /8-x-8-removable-floor-door-recessed-vinyl-carpet (purchasable:false, $0.00); the two attic ladders, /36-x-36-roof-hatch and /24-x-36-flush-aluminum-floor-hatch (freight class); and the nine slugs carrying 1-3 required modifier groups. checkout.customFields is [] — VERIFIED via the public, unauthenticated GET /api/storefront/form-fields, which reports BESTCA's only two custom shipping fields (field_26 'Estimated Ship Date', field_28 'Delivery Availability') as required:false. That endpoint is the source the DOM is not: it reports BESTUS's field_36 as required:true even though the markup carries no `required` attribute. No personaOverrides needed — the shared Canadian fixture persona (Waterloo ON N2L4T8) is the right market, cy.select('Canada')/('ON') both resolve, and the postcode quotes carrier shipping fine despite BCData reporting weight:null on all 15 pdp.popular products (BESTUS reports 6.14 LBS for the same panel — check the catalog's shipping weights in BC admin if quotes ever come back empty). Unlike BESTUS, BESTCA's 'Save this address in my address book' ships CHECKED, so ensureSaveAddressUnchecked() does real work here rather than acting as a guard; the address book held 8 entries across two back-to-back runs (Sept 22 2026) and must not grow. /checkout is BigCommerce-served and untouched by the Snap theme drift that governs BESTCA's PLP/PDP, but it is NOT the same checkout-js build as BESTUS and needs two selector overrides (both found Sept 23 2026, by dumping every step container's className at each stage rather than guessing): (a) activeStepClass is 'checkout-step--current', because this build never puts 'active' on any step at all — and unlike BESTUS's cumulative 'active' it marks exactly ONE step and moves it along, so payment carrying it is a stronger signal here, not a weaker one; (b) storeCreditCheckbox is null, because BigCommerce renders #useStoreCredit only for a customer who actually holds store credit and this one holds none. storeCreditOverlay is deliberately left at its default — it is an interlock placeOrder.js relies on, and nulling it would remove a guard on a store whose config sets placeOrder. PRICING: the QA customer group zeroes the product (listPrice/salePrice 0 against originalPrice 57.99, same arrangement as BESTUS) AND is offered a genuine type:'freeshipping' option, so a fully correct BESTCA checkout is payable-ZERO (subtotal 0 + shipping 0 + tax 0 = grand 0). That is what retired checkout.cy.js's old `shippingCostTotal > 0` proxy in favour of comparing the total against the selected option's own cost. Note the consequence for arming: a $0 order needs no store credit, so the interlocks in placeOrder.js were designed around a balance this store does not have — re-verify them before ever running an armed BESTCA order. RESOLVED SITE DEFECT (raised with BESTCA devs Sept 22 2026, fix confirmed live Sept 23 2026): an inline script on /checkout defined function stopFunction2(){ stopFunction2(myVar2); } — calling ITSELF instead of clearInterval(myVar2), a copy-paste slip from the correct stopFunction() 25 lines above — so showTime2()'s 1-second setInterval threw RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded on the payment step, for the suite and for every real customer reaching that step. Worth keeping on record because of what it hid: the RangeError fired about a second into assertPaymentStep()'s 60s retry window and failed the test first, so the activeStepClass drift in (a) above was completely masked and only surfaced once the theme was fixed. A store can carry more than one checkout problem at a time, and the loudest one is not necessarily the config one.
